place.source_title: Mac's Super Service Station, Traverse City

brief: A small streamline service station: pale green enamel-panelled walls with rounded corners, a flat roof, two service bays and an office with a stepped tower, fuel pumps in front. One photo. Older than 1970: a pre-war main-street building; no newer example of this type on the lake. Foundations taken deeper than needed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: Mac's Super Service (Traverse City, 1935): an Art Deco service station clad in cream and green glazed terra-cotta tile, 'WASHING GREASING BATTERIES TIRES' moulded in the frieze, a stepped deco tower at the corner entrance, three service bays; now a repair shop

why.note: 1930s oil companies' streamline / deco stations in washable glazed tile
